text: The Patriots' roster underwent minor adjustments this week with linebacker Jose Ramirez re-signing to the practice squad while offensive lineman Jacob Rizy and punter Bryce Baringer were released, but the more pressing concern remains on the field after New England's 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday night in Chicago—a defeat made worse by the team's continued struggles with turnover differential, one of Mike Vrabel's four pillars of team identity that proved costly against Caleb Williams and Chicago's offense. Drake Maye's performance came without starting guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown due to injury, though running back Rhamondre Stevenson provided a bright spot by reaching a career high in receiving yards and continuing his pattern of doing the little things that keep him on pace for his sixth consecutive season of 100-plus carries. The loss came despite Stevenson's production, leaving the Patriots facing a Notre Dame-Navy matchup this week at Gillette Stadium—a historic college football rivalry making its first appearance at the stadium—while New England works to shore up its glaring turnover issues that have become the difference between winning and losing.
